articles.title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out
articles.summary: Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good life. Benjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit.

articles.title: Turkey gets a glowup: how a Chinese BBQ spot remade the Thanksgiving bird
articles.summary: Chicago’s Sun Wah BBQ started a new Turkey Day tradition for immigrants and other neighbors: allowing them to bring in their fowl and roast it in the fragrant Hong Kong-style. Tell us: do you have a special new year food tradition?
body: Behind an Uptown Chicago facade of glass and green-glazed bricks, rows of mahogany-red ducks glisten.

This neighborhood is sometimes called “New Chinatown”, sometimes “Little Vietnam ”. And this tidy restaurant is Sun Wah BBQ, which Eric and Lynda Cheng opened in 1987. Today, it’s also an unlikely Thanksgiving destination.

Every November, customers bring their own turkeys to Sun Wah to be prepared in the style of a Hong Kong roast duck. This year, the Cheng family will roast close to 200 turkeys, thanks to a TikTok video that increased demand. But this annual tradition, turning pale workaday turkeys into gorgeously lacquered holiday centerpieces, began as an informal favor about two decades ago.

articles.title: Inside WNBA Star Cameron Brink and Ben Felter’s Stanford Wedding—and Her Four Bridal Looks
articles.summary: Six years after an “athlete mingle survey” brought them together during Covid, the WNBA star Cameron Brink and the robotics founder Ben Felter tied the knot at Stanford’s Memorial Church before celebrating along the California coast in Half Moon Bay.
body: WNBA basketball player Cameron Brink and rower-turned-robotics founder Ben Felter were the rare college students who were able to find love at the height of Covid. Since they were athletes, the Stanford freshmen were in the tiny group allowed on campus during the fall of 2020. “The only people I socialized with were my basketball teammates—until the upperclassmen on my team had us fill out an ‘athlete mingle survey,’” Cameron says.

She begrudgingly filled out the form, was matched with Ben, and later received an email with the subject, “attempting to mingle.” In the message, Ben wrote: “I wanted to chat you up but thought DMs were a bit creepy, so here’s my number.” Cameron—who goes by Cam—says she jumped up and down in her room, elated that he was gentlemanly enough to reach out with his number.

“From there, we had three dates where Ben showed me his hometown of Palo Alto, and he asked me to be his girlfriend five days before we won a national championship,” says Cam. “He is my forever good luck charm.” She adds her friends and teammates Lexie and Lacie Hull were the ones who paired them together and is “forever grateful for their vision.”

articles.title: The Golden Rules of Affordable Family Travel, Illustrated by Mona Chalabi
articles.summary: The Pulitzer Prize-winning writer and illustrator brings the fundamentals of affordable family travel—shared by our network of well-traveled parents—to life.
body: Take it from an immigrant: this holiday is full of weird contradictions. Of course, there’s the annual reminder of colonization which requires a careful forgetting of the people who have been colonized. And then there’s the financial aspect of it. At first blush, it seems like the least capitalist holiday of the year—there isn’t the expense of Christmas or Hanukkah gift-giving or the extravagance of Halloween candy. Yet the holiday also marks the start of one of the year's busiest travel seasons when families are taking great expense to reunite, vacation, and explore outside of their every day lives.
Keep reading for the tips and tricks of affordable family travel, road-tested by the experts and illustrated by Mona Chalabi.

articles.title: You Can Now Buy A-Listers’ Favorite Quiet Luxury Handbag Brand for Less
articles.summary: Celeb-favorite handbag brand Demellier is offering 20% off all its bestsellers this Black Friday. Shop styles seen on EmRata, Katie Holmes, and Kate Middleton.
body: There are certain brands that have claimed pride of place in our wardrobes without the gimmicks of internet-breaking campaigns or showy logos, and Demellier is one such example. Launching in its current state in 2017, the London-based brand has become a constant in the wardrobes of fashion editors and A-listers alike, including Emily Ratajkowski, Anne Hathaway, and Katie Holmes. And while the brand rarely discounts its goods, Black Friday is one of the few exceptions, and this year the sale is looking better than ever.

Through November 30, Demellier is offering shoppers 20% off sitewide—the discount automatically applied at checkout. It’s a one-week window of being able to nab the brand’s sellout styles—from the capacious Stockholm to the compact, Katie Holmes-approved Siena—for less.

articles.title: These Stylish Meta Oakley Smart Glasses Are $120 Off for Black Friday

There's is no shortage of smart glasses on the market right now, but many of them have an awkward, clunky aesthetic that doesn’t exactly blend into your everyday style.
body: While they have similar core features to the Meta Ray-Ban Gen 2 (also 25% off ahead of the holiday), these frames are sportier, and unlike the Ray-Bans, they shoot video in 3K rather than 1080p. They also have a bigger battery designed to last all day (up to eight hours on a charge, and five additional charges from the case, for a total of 48 hours). In addition, the two open-ear speakers have been repositioned, allowing for audio to be directed more effectively towards the ears with less sound leakage.

Available in a range of stylish frame and lens colors, PCMag dubs these the best “smart glasses for Instagram addicts” given their social-focused design; users can use the embedded cameras to snap POV videos or photos and upload them seamlessly to Facebook or Instagram. They have a 12MP camera and come with 32GB of flash storage.

If you want a pair of smart glasses but have been on the fence due to mixed feedback about sound and battery life, the Oakley Meta HSTN smart glasses are a more advanced model that solves both of those problems with upgrades that outdo the Ray-Bans while allowing you to film and shoot POV videos on the go. Now $120 off, they're also at an all-time low price.
